claims.text: As of 28 July 2026, a total of 109 deaths and 360 injuries have been reported nationwide. The majority of casualties resulted from house collapses and flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall. Additionally, 796 houses have been damaged, either fully or partially, while 379 livestock have perished.

OCHA, 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 2' (as of 10 August 2026, infographic sourced to NDMA's Monsoon situation report covering 26 June-9 August 2026, plus PMD and WFP data): 'Deaths: 153,' 'Injured: 457,' 'Houses Damaged: 1,339 total (432 Fully Damaged and 907 Partially Damaged),' 'Livestock Lost: 576.'

NDMA, Monsoon 2026 Daily Situation Report No. 47 (11 August 2026): cumulative casualties and injuries table, 'From 26 June 2026 to 11 August 2026' -- Grand Total Deceased 155 (52 male, 30 female, 73 children), Grand Total Injured 460 (195 male, 113 female, 152 children). Cumulative damage table for the same period: Houses Full 432, Partial 909, Total 1,341; Livestock Perished 580. The last-24-hours entry for 11 August records 1 injury (Narowal, Punjab), no new deaths, and 1 partial house damaged.

NDMA Monsoon 2026 Daily Situation Report No. 49 (covering 1300 hrs 12 August - 1300 hrs 13 August 2026): cumulative deaths unchanged at 155 (52 male, 30 female, 73 children); injured risen to 468 (up from 460, +8 in the last 24 hours, all in Rajanpur, Punjab); houses damaged (cumulative) risen to 1,345 (432 fully damaged, 913 partially damaged, up from 1,341); livestock perished unchanged at 580; cumulative rescue operations since 26 June 2026: 1,111 operations, 8,700 persons rescued.

OCHA's 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 2' (as of 10 August 2026, sourced from NDMA's situation reporting covering 26 June-9 August 2026): 153 deaths, 457 injured, 1,339 houses damaged (432 fully, 907 partially), 576 livestock lost, with severe impacts in Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. WHO (12 August 2026) states the health sector stands ready to activate the Monsoon and Flood Contingency Plan 2026 to assist 1.8 million people in high-risk areas.

NDMA's live Monsoon 2026 SITREP dashboard, as of 18 August 2026 (cumulative, 26 June-18 August 2026): Grand Total Deceased 161 (54 male, 32 female, 75 children), Grand Total Injured 473 (196 male, 118 female, 159 children) -- up from 155 deaths / 468 injured as of NDMA Daily Situation Report No. 49 (13 August 2026). Cumulative houses damaged 1,355 total (433 fully damaged, 922 partially damaged); livestock perished 585. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa recorded the highest death toll (67) and injury count (92); Punjab recorded 54 deaths and 341 injured; Gilgit-Baltistan recorded the most housing damage (403 structures). Separately, NDMA's numbered Daily Situation Report No. 51 (15 August 2026, covering 1300 hrs 14 August-1300 hrs 15 August 2026), fetched directly, confirms cumulative Grand Total Deceased 157 and Grand Total Injured 469 as of that date, and cumulative houses damaged of 1,349 (433 full, 916 partial) and livestock perished 585 -- consistent with the trend shown on the live dashboard, and reflecting NDMA's own numbered situation-report series had progressed to Report No. 51 without being previously captured in this record. reliefweb.int/country/pak again returned HTTP 403 Forbidden and no OCHA 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 3' was found via search.

NDMA's live Monsoon 2026 SITREP dashboard, as of 20 August 2026 (cumulative, 26 June-20 August 2026): Grand Total Deceased 163 (55 male, 33 female, 75 children), Grand Total Injured 483 (200 male, 122 female, 161 children) -- up from 161 deaths / 473 injured as of 18 August 2026. Housing damage: 1,499 houses affected (949 partially damaged, 550 destroyed); 1,413 livestock lost. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa recorded the highest death toll (69) and Punjab the most injuries (349).

NDMA's live Monsoon 2026 SITREP dashboard, as of 21 August 2026 (cumulative, 26 June-21 August 2026): Grand Total Deceased 164 (55 male, 33 female, 76 children), Grand Total Injured 484 (200 male, 122 female, 162 children) -- up from 163 deaths and 483 injuries as of 20 August. Cumulative housing damage: 1,517 houses affected (966 partially damaged, 551 destroyed); 1,419 livestock lost. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa recorded the highest death toll (70) and Punjab the most injuries (349); Gilgit-Baltistan recorded the most housing damage (535 structures). The last 24 hours (21 August) recorded 1 new death and 1 new injury, both in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

NDMA's live Monsoon 2026 SITREP dashboard, as of 22 August 2026 (cumulative, 26 June-22 August 2026): Grand Total Deceased 165 (56 male, 33 female, 76 children), Grand Total Injured 496 (206 male, 128 female, 162 children) -- up from 164 deaths and 484 injuries as of 21 August. Cumulative housing damage: 1,567 houses affected (1,005 partially damaged, 562 destroyed); 1,436 livestock lost. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa recorded the highest death toll (70) and injury count (95); Gilgit-Baltistan recorded the most housing damage (535 structures) and livestock lost (910). Cumulative rescue operations reached 1,161, with 9,435 persons rescued and 93 relief camps established.

NDMA and PDMA Punjab have moved from advisory to an active flood alert for the Chenab, Jhelum and Ravi rivers from 29 July-05 August, with evacuations already being directed in low-lying and riverbank areas.

NDMA's live Monsoon 2026 SITREP dashboard, as of 24 August 2026 (cumulative 26 June-24 August), records 166 deaths and 500 injuries nationwide, up from 165 deaths and 496 injuries on 22 August, with cumulative houses damaged rising to 1,597 (568 destroyed, 1,029 partially damaged) and livestock lost to 1,442.

NDMA's live Monsoon 2026 SITREP dashboard, as of 25 August 2026 (cumulative, 26 June-25 August 2026): Grand Total Deceased 169, Grand Total Injured 500 -- up from 166 deaths and 500 injuries as of 24 August. Cumulative housing damage: 1,601 houses affected (571 destroyed, 1,030 partially damaged); livestock lost 1,442 (unchanged). Cumulative rescue operations reached 1,164, with 9,439 persons rescued, 93 relief camps and 66 medical camps established. Provincial death toll: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 70, Punjab 55, Sindh 17, Azad Jammu & Kashmir 16, Balochistan 8, Islamabad Capital Territory 2, Gilgit-Baltistan 1.

NDMA's live Monsoon 2026 SITREP dashboard, as of 28 August 2026 (cumulative, 26 June-28 August 2026): Grand Total Deceased 169, Grand Total Injured 500 -- unchanged since 25 August. Cumulative housing damage rose to 1,653 houses affected (571 destroyed, 1,082 partially damaged), up from 1,601 (571 destroyed, 1,030 partially damaged) on 25 August; livestock lost unchanged at 1,442. Cumulative rescue operations remain at 1,164, with 9,439 persons rescued, 93 relief camps and 66 medical camps established -- unchanged from 25 August. Provincial death toll unchanged: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 70, Punjab 55, Sindh 17, Azad Jammu & Kashmir 16, Balochistan 8, Islamabad Capital Territory 2, Gilgit-Baltistan 1.

OCHA's 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 1' infographic (as of 03 Aug 2026, posted to ReliefWeb 3 August 2026) states: 'Based on NDMA Monsoon situation report covering from 26 June to 2 August 2026, monsoon-related incidents have resulted in 126 deaths and 416 injuries across Pakistan... In addition, 1,119 houses have been damaged (352 fully damaged and 767 partially damaged), while 508 livestock have perished due to the monsoon-related hazards. The most affected areas in terms of housing damage include Gilgit-Baltistan, Balochistan, Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and AJ&K.'

description: Heavy monsoon rains since 26 June 2026 have triggered flash floods, riverine flooding and house collapses across Pakistan, hitting Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Gilgit-Baltistan hardest. Pakistan's National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) records a cumulative 169 deaths and 500 injuries nationwide from 26 June to 28 August 2026 -- unchanged for the past three days -- with 1,653 houses damaged (up from 1,601 on 25 August) and 1,442 livestock lost; Khyber Pakhtunkhwa carries the heaviest provincial death toll at 70, followed by Punjab at 55. Relief operations remain active nationwide: NDMA teams have carried out 1,164 rescue operations, rescued 9,439 people and established 93 relief camps and 66 medical camps, all steady since 25 August, and WHO stands ready to activate a contingency plan to assist 1.8 million people in high-risk areas.

impact.summary: NDMA's live Monsoon 2026 SITREP dashboard puts the cumulative toll from 26 June to 28 August 2026 at 169 deaths and 500 injuries, unchanged since 25 August, while cumulative housing damage continues to rise, now standing at 1,653 houses affected (571 destroyed, 1,082 partially damaged) and 1,442 livestock lost. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has recorded the most deaths (70), followed by Punjab (55). NDMA teams have conducted 1,164 rescue operations, rescued 9,439 people and established 93 relief camps and 66 medical camps -- all unchanged over the past three days.
